prompt: We're a mid-size financial services company (around 500 employees) and we've decided to build our own private cloud instead of continuing to pay AWS bills that keep climbing. We need to support about 500 VMs, we've already bought Cisco Nexus 9000 switches and want to use ACI, and our storage team is leaning toward Ceph. We need to stay compliant with PCI-DSS and SOC2. Can you design the architecture for this? Include networking, storage, compute, identity, monitoring, and automation. We have a small but competent ops team of 6 people.

assertions.name: mentions_openstack
assertions.description: Recommends OpenStack or explains platform choice for IaaS

assertions.name: cisco_aci_integration
assertions.description: Covers Cisco ACI fabric design and integration with the cloud platform (EPGs, contracts, APIC)

assertions.name: ceph_storage_design
assertions.description: Designs Ceph storage architecture with pool layout, replication, or erasure coding

assertions.name: pci_dss_compliance
assertions.description: Addresses PCI-DSS compliance with specific controls or segmentation requirements

assertions.name: identity_management
assertions.description: Covers identity/auth solution (LDAP, FreeIPA, Keycloak, AD, or similar)

assertions.name: monitoring_stack
assertions.description: Specifies a monitoring/observability stack (Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, etc.)

assertions.name: automation_strategy
assertions.description: Covers IaC/automation approach (Ansible, Terraform/OpenTofu, or similar)

assertions.name: team_size_appropriate
assertions.description: Architecture is realistic for a 6-person ops team (mentions operational simplicity, automation to reduce burden, or explicitly addresses team capacity)

assertions.name: compute_sizing
assertions.description: Includes compute node sizing or hardware recommendations for 500 VMs
